addedCourses: Uses spatial engineering, GIS and remote sensing in disaster, agricultural and environmental projects. Description-only evidence supports real spatial analysis, not hydraulic/structural engineering design.

Develops differential/difference-equation systems, frequency representations, feedback and stability. Actual engineering mathematics and signal-system analysis; no claim of structural statics, fluid mechanics or hydraulic load calculation.

Develops specifications, concept selection, user investigation, production plans and prototypes for consumer products. Genuine design methods and material/circularity inquiry, not civil-structure or hydraulic infrastructure design.
academicFinding: Full consideration of Building with Nature intervention/model-wall work, water appraisal, groundwater geophysics, material stress/strain foundations, treatment chemistry, Linear Systems, Spatial Planning and consumer-product prototyping. These are genuine technical/design contributions. The dominant practice remains environmental investigation and appraisal supported by mathematics and general design methods, without a sequence that formulates and tests load-bearing structures, soil/foundation systems, hydraulic behaviour and engineered infrastructure designs. That programme-level gap persists after strengthening; it is not a licence, title, exact-equivalence or matching-course-quota test. A thematic response to flood adaptation alone cannot establish comparability to this broad Civil Engineering target.
